title: R' Yehudah ben Lakrat

paragraphs: Mentioned in Sukkah 4:6, reporting an aggadic teaching in the name of R' Shmuel bar Nachman. At the beginning of Eichah Rabbati chapter 4, the statement appears with Rabbi Chiya Kara as its attribution [supplied וגרם ר׳ חייא קרא].

notes.text: The source prints וגרם ר׳ חייא קרא. Whether this gives a reading “Rabbi Chiya Kara,” and the exact function of קרא, remain unresolved.

The saved whole Torat Emet EichahRabbah4 scalar3 explicitly has Rabbi Chiyya Kara בשם Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman. It supports the attributed-name reading beside supplied וגרם ר׳ חייא קרא, contextually perhaps וגרס, reads; it does not prove Hyman’s printed מ/ס history. Kara remains a byname, with Scripture-reader a possible explanation rather than an admitted identity. Lakrat and indexed Lakrach remain distinct. The Sukkah4:6 occurrence is not newly inspected; its Yehudah and Shmuel title abbreviations remain R', while the matched Eichah Chiyya title is explicitly Rabbi.

In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 4:6, Rabbi Yudah bar Lakara reports the teaching in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name. In the parallel opening of Eichah Rabbah 4, Rabbi Chiyya Kara reports the same teaching about thickened wine and white glass from Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman. Hyman prints Lakrat in the heading. These passages document the names of the transmitters as they appear in their respective witnesses.
